title: Authorization & Resource Ownership
intro: Applies to: owned-resource handlers, capability-gated routes, guards, Form Request `authorize()`. Authorization failures are critical; every MUST here is a security rule.

entries.rule: Authorization **MUST** derive from the authenticated principal, never from request input. A handler that trusts a `user_id`, `team_id`, or `role` from the request body is broken.

signals: a handler that trusts a `user_id`, `team_id`, or `role` from the request body

checks.coverage: Flags a handler or controller that reads `user_id`, `team_id` or `role` from request input. Misses an actor id under another key name.

entries.rule: Every endpoint touching owned data **MUST** scope its lookup by the actor (IDOR protection: stopping one user from reading another's record by changing an id). "Fetch by id, then check" is not scoping; the gate lives in the lookup itself.
entries.why: IDOR protection: stopping one user from reading another's record by changing an id
allowed_in: query handlers for genuinely public, ownerless data

sections.heading: Ownership gates live in model lookups

entries.rule: An owned-resource handler **MUST** resolve actor plus resource through a model method that asserts membership/ownership and throws: `Team::findByIdForMemberOrFail($teamId, $userId)` for reads, `findByIdForAdminOrFail(...)` or an `*AsAdmin(...)` write method for privileged writes. Never `find()` plus a manual check in the handler.
allowed_in: query handlers for genuinely public, ownerless data

signals: `find()` plus a manual check in the handler

checks.coverage: Flags a `find()` call on a model inside a handler class. Cannot tell whether the model is owned or whether the check after it is an ownership check, so each finding needs review.

entries.rule: The gate **MUST** throw a domain exception that renders itself as 403. Controllers **MUST NOT** build 403 responses inline.

signals: a controller that builds a 403 response inline

checks.coverage: Flags a 403 status code passed to a response or abort call inside a controller class. Misses a 403 built in a helper the controller calls.

entries.note: Authentication is route middleware (`auth:sanctum`, `verified`). Authorization is the domain gate above. A Form Request `authorize()` returning `true` is correct under this split; **do not** move ownership checks into Form Requests.

entries.rule: Every Form Request still **MUST** define `authorize()` explicitly (even when it returns `true`) alongside `rules()`.

signals: a Form Request with no `authorize()` of its own

checks.coverage: Flags a Form Request class that does not declare `authorize()` itself. Counts an inherited `authorize()` as missing.

entries.rule: Capability-gated endpoints **MUST** use ability middleware with a typed constant (`'abilities:'.PublishingAbility::NAME`), never a string literal.

signals: ability middleware given as a string literal instead of a typed constant like `'abilities:'.PublishingAbility::NAME`

checks.coverage: Flags an `abilities:` middleware argument that is one whole string literal. Misses a string built from a variable that is not a constant.

entries.rule: Separate application surfaces **MUST** use separate guards; an admin panel authenticates through its own guard plus an access check (`canAccessPanel()`-style), never the customer app's guard or role enums (see `isolation.md`).

signals: an admin panel on the customer app's guard
an admin panel that reads the customer app's role enums
an admin panel with no `canAccessPanel()`-style access check

checks.coverage: Forbids the admin panel layer from depending on the customer app's role enums. Does not see which guard a panel is configured with.

entries.note: `authorize(): true` on a Form Request (the split above).
A query handler for genuinely public, ownerless data.
